name: r6b_tou_bank_lead_follows_primary_heat__v4
description: Heating mirror of r6b_tou_bank_lead_follows_primary__v4: a winter peak starts at 16:15, the house is at 71 F and banking toward the 76 F comfort ceiling means 5 F of heat. Primary engine v4 (v3 live as the comparison engine), a realistic 3.5 F per hour furnace, 30 F outside and a 0.05 leak: the lead comes from v4's OWN house model (thermal mass and sun included), stepped with the furnace fully on against the forecast, not from a first-order formula (Issue #1517). That model needs about 493 minutes (566 with the 1.15 safety factor), so the lead hits the 240-minute cap and the window opens at 12:15, before this scenario's 13:00 start. The bank is on from the first moment: the thermostat is told 76 F at 13:00 with no 68 F comfort write first, the plan names the 12:15 window, and the 13:05 check and the half-hour cycles re-assert 76 F.

events.note: The 13:30 plan cycle (the v4 bank window has not started).
End of run: after the 13:55 check opened the bank.

assertions.reason: The window (12:15) is already open when the scenario starts, so the bank applies at once.
The 13:00 setup tells the thermostat the 76 F bank setpoint, without the 68 F comfort setpoint first (issue #1393; the heating mirror).
The 14:00 cycle inside the open bank re-asserts the 76 F bank setpoint once, without the 68 F comfort setpoint first.

The window the plan shows starts at the 240-minute cap: v4's own house model needs about 493 minutes (566 with the safety factor) to bank 5 F in 30 F weather (Issue #1517; the first-order leak lead also hit the cap, the leak-unaware lead said 13:56).
Banking toward the 76 F comfort ceiling.
The plan list has no pre-heat step: the window opened at 12:15, before now, so it is already running.

verdict.summary: The heating bank opens by the primary engine (v4) rate, and the plan and thermostat agree on when
verdict.observed_behavior: Window 12:15 (the 240-minute cap; v4's model needs about 493 min raw, 566 min with the safety factor); 76 F written at 13:00 and re-asserted at 13:04:59, 13:30 and 14:00.
verdict.expected_behavior: Mirror of the cooling bank: the lead is v4's own house model (thermal mass, sun, leak), not a first-order formula (Issue #1517). Re-derived 2026-11-11 with the owner's approval (second re-derivation for #1517): the window and writes are unchanged from the first re-derivation (the first-order leak lead already hit the 240-minute cap), but the reason changed: v4's own model needs about 493 min raw / 566 min with the 1.15 safety factor, so even the cap is short - tracked separately (the owner estimated about 450).
